goal: Hang all three mugs by their handles on the mug rack (cup holder) with the arm(s), then return the arm home.
instruction_templates: Hang all the mugs on the mug rack.
success: For each of mug0, mug1, mug2: root z is more than 0.045 m above the mug's initial root z (is_lift z_threshold=0.045, strict), i.e. the mug has been lifted at least 4.5 cm from where it started.

For each mug: at least one of its active functional points tagged 'handle' has world z > 0.9 m (is_A_functional_point_higher_than_z, absolute z in the simulation world frame; the exact reference frame/table height is not determinable statically, so this is an absolute height).

For each mug: the handle point's local +z axis is within 60 degrees (strict <60) of the rack's passive functional point 'handle_support_point' local +z axis (is_axis_aligned with functional_point_A='handle' (active), functional_point_B='handle_support_point' (passive)).
For each mug: the handle point's local +x axis is within 60 degrees of either the support point's local +x or its local -x axis (parallel or anti-parallel).

For each mug: the handle point (active) is within 0.045 m (3D Euclidean distance, strict <) of at least one 'handle_support_point' (passive) of cup_holder (is_A_functional_point_close_to_B_functional_point threshold=0.045, no orientation check on that one). Each mug is tested against any support point of the rack independently; the code does not require different mugs to use different hooks.
All target robots back at start end-effector pose: |dx|,|dy|,|dz| each <= 0.15 m and rotation <= 20 degrees (all_robot_back_to_origin defaults).
evaluation: Checked after every action; all conditions for all three mugs plus the arm-home condition must hold at the same step; the first such step is success. Fails at step_lim=800 actions. No early-fail rule. Because success requires arms back home and handles within 4.5 cm of the support points with no release condition, the mugs must be resting on the hooks (they will fall otherwise) when the arm is home. Process score (partial only, scores 15/40/100) tracks mugs hung with grippers open (>=0.8), also requiring each previously hung mug's handle point not to move more than 0.005 m since the last check.
objects: mug0, mug1, mug2: mugs (category mug, model indices in {10,11,12,13,14}, 3 chosen with duplicates allowed), on the table, x in [-0.45,0.45], y in [-0.25,0.02] (m), random yaw in [15,165] degrees, margin 0.05 m. Each has an active 'handle' functional point.

cup_holder: mug rack (Geometry, category cup_holder, model index 1), 1, on the table, x in [-0.20,0.20], y in [0.0,0.05], random yaw within +/-25 degrees, 0.03 m margin. It has passive 'handle_support_point' functional points (hooks).

Clutter: 20 distractor objects (category_unique) on the table, x in [-0.6,0.6], y in [-0.5,0.5], yaw +/-30 deg, margin 0.015; keep-out area x[-0.35,0.35], y[-0.5,-0.4]. They are not part of the reward.
end_requirements: Target arms back within 0.15 m per axis and 20 degrees of start end-effector pose at the moment of success; mugs must be on the hooks at that moment.
notes: The z > 0.9 handle height is an absolute number, whose consistency with the world frame (table height, env origin offsets) cannot be verified statically; it just means the handle must be on the elevated hooks. Handle orientation tolerance is loose (60 degrees) but position tolerance to the hook point is 4.5 cm. Mug yaw is random in [15,165] degrees so handles point in different directions. Hook assignment among mugs is unconstrained by code.
